verifyNotes: node tools/verify-page.mjs --drafts /networking/dns/ run from PowerShell on the issue-75-dns worktree (branch verified via `git branch --show-current` before and during the run: issue-75-dns). Printed summary: FAIL /networking/dns/ words=3035 code=14 fig=2 lh(p/a/bp/seo)=91/100/100/100, single failure 'placeholder text: NEEDS_MARKUS' (expected per the gauntlet note until the owner supplies a byline/legal name - confirmed as three NEEDS_MARKUS hits: byline, footer copyright, and one more, all pre-existing owner-input placeholders, not new). report.json confirms: words 3035 (was 2997 in round 2), codeBlocks 14 (unchanged - this round added no new code), figures 2 (was 1 - Figure 2 confirmed present), h1 1, internalLinks 27, mobileOverflowPx 0, consoleErrors [], consoleWarnings [], broken []. lighthouse.json: performance 91 (down from round 2's 94 but still >=90; the failing sub-audits are the same generic dev-server ones as round 2 - first-contentful-paint 0.79, total-blocking-time 0.83, max-potential-fid 0.16, bf-cache 0, network-dependency-tree 0, document-latency 0.5 - none article-specific, consistent with the page simply having more DOM/SVG now). Screenshots read in full for this round: all 18 mobile-light + 18 mobile-dark parts (up from 17, matching the added figure and +38 words), desktop-light parts 1, 2, 9, 10, desktop-dark parts 9, 10. Spot-checked the previously-fixed round-1 defects for regression: Figure 1's annotation text still clears the 'you' lifeline (mobile-light/dark part04), the record-type table's Stores column still shows complete untruncated phrases for all six rows including AAAA/CNAME/NS/MX (mobile-light part08), and the 'iana.org auth' loop still clears its label - no regressions from round 2's fixes.
justification: This round's only substantive change is the new Figure 2 (a four-row 'signal you observe -> what it means' vertical checklist in the failure-modes section, mirroring the article's own closing decision-procedure bullets), and it is technically well-built: markup checked against WRITER_GUIDE section 5's hard rules (no blank line inside the figure, viewBox starts at '0 0', role='img' plus title/desc with page-unique ids 'dnsfail-title'/'dnsfail-desc' referenced by aria-labelledby, no literal fill/stroke colours, figcaption last child) and all satisfied. Semantic colouring is correct and deliberate: the three genuinely-broken outcomes (TIMEOUT, NXDOMAIN, SERVFAIL) all use `d-box-bad`/`d-text-bad` (confirmed red in both themes, mobile-light/dark part15 and desktop-light/dark part10), while the 'not actually an error' STALE ANSWER row uses `d-box-warn` (amber box, confirmed in both themes) with plain bold text rather than a fabricated `d-text-warn` class - correct, since that class does not exist in global.css (only `--d-warn` and `.d-box-warn` are defined; `d-text-good`/`d-text-bad`/`d-text-accent` are the only coloured text classes the shell ships). At 390px in both themes the whole 360-viewBox drawing fits inside the phone column with no scroll and no faded edge, every label is legible at d-small/d-bold sizing, and nothing the caption references is cut off - it passes the mobile legibility check cleanly. On desktop it has the same minor, non-blocking cosmetic issue Figure 1 has always had (a 360-unit viewBox rendering well under the width of its figure frame, so it reads as a narrower island in a wide column) - unchanged, shared shell CSS, integrator-owned, not new. On the structural question this round exists to answer: Figure 2 is a genuine, correctly-executed improvement, but it only partially addresses what was actually flagged. The round-2 major issue named two things - the four-times-repeated BuildQuery/ReadName boilerplate and the fact that 'the record-type, TTL and failure-mode sections - most of the page - have no visual break at all' - and its fixLooksLike asked for both a de-duplication pass and one added figure. Only the figure was added; the repetition is completely untouched (BuildQuery still appears five times - id=walk, the exercise-1 solution, id=records, id=failures, and the exercise-2 solution - and ReadName still appears in full three times, at essentially the same line counts as round 2: id=records ~96 lines, the exercise-2 solution ~84 lines). And Figure 2's placement, while it correctly echoes the closing bullets, lands at only around the 83% mark of the page (mobile part 15 of 18), immediately after those bullets and right before exercise 2 - it does not touch the record-type section (the six-row Stores/RDATA table plus the ~22-line id=addresses and ~96-line id=records code blocks) or the TTL section at all, and it comes after, not before, the largest remaining code block in the failure-modes section itself (id=failures, ~108 lines). By line count, roughly 290 of the body's ~720 lines (from the start of 'The record types, and what each one actually stores' through the end of the failure-mode bullets, right up to Figure 2) - about 40% of the article, containing the table and three of its four largest code blocks - still has zero visual break of any kind. So the structural concern is meaningfully but only partially addressed: the article now bookends with two diagrams instead of one, and the failure-modes section specifically reads better because the new figure gives the reader a fast visual lookup distinct from the prose bullets above it (not pure duplication - a flowchart-style quick reference is a different reading mode than a paragraph), but the middle of the article that was explicitly named as the biggest gap - record types and TTL - remains exactly as bare as it was in round 1, and the repetition that was called the 'main reason the design score is not yet at the 8.5 pass bar' in round 2 has not been touched. A fresh full pass over everything else - headings (still five plain H2s matching the on-page TOC, confirmed via desktop-light part01, no skipped levels), both exercises' solution collapses, the sources list and footer, and the surrounding prose - turned up no new issues.
